sentences.text:
Opposite Party
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Pradeep Kumar Srivastava
For the Petitioner : Mrs. Jasvindar Mazumdar, Adv.
For the State : Ms. Lily Sahay, Addl. P.P. Order No.04/Dated- 12.07.2024 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. The petitioner has been made an accused in connection with Rajganj P.S. Case No. 17 of 2024 registered for the offences under Sections 447, 376, 511 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, pending in the Court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Dhanbad.

3. As per FIR, the informant, who lives with her children in a rented house, alleged that on 02.04.2024 at about 10:00 AM, while she was doing domestic work, petitioner came to her house under the pretext of collecting an overdue electricity bill.
He forcibly entered and outraged her modesty.
When she pulled him and raised an alarm, he threatened to kill her if she continued.
As villagers arrived, petitioner tried to flee away on his two-wheeler but was surrounded and caught by the villagers.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all rather he has been falsely implicated in this case.
It is further submitted that it is a case of attempt to rape.

As alleged in the F.I.R., the allegation is that present petitioner present himself to be the staff of the electricity house came to the house of the informant claiming electricity bill, he entered into the house of informant and laid her down with a view to commit rape with her,
when she raised an alarm, the accused petitioner had threatened to kill her.
The petitioner is languishing in Judicial Custody since 03.04.2024 without any rhymes and reasons.
Petitioner has no criminal antecedent.

Petitioner undertakes to cooperate in the trial of the case by remaining physically present as and when required and shall not indulge in any manner in tampering with the prosecution evidences or influencing the witnesses of prosecution.
Hence, the petitioner may be extended the privilege of bail.

5. On the other hand, learned Addl.P.P appearing for the State has opposed the prayer for bail of the petitioner and submitted that petitioner was really not any employee of the electricity department.
He has taken advantage of the situation and attempted to commit rape with the victim.

Hence,
petitioner does not deserve bail.

sentences.text: 1 6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of allegation coupled with the materials available against the petitioner and period of custody of the petitioner, I am inclined to release the petitioner on bail.

Accordingly, the petitioner named above is directed to be released on bail on furnishing of bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Twenty five thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Dhanbad in connection with Rajganj P.S. Case No. 17 of 2024 subject to the conditions:-
(1) Petitioner shall remain physically present on each and every date till the conclusion of the trial of this case unless prevented from sufficient cause to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court.
(2) Petitioner shall not indulge in any or other similar offence till the conclusion of the trial.
(3) Petitioner shall not indulge in tampering with the prosecution evidences or influencing the prosecution witnesses.
(Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Sachin Rafique Ansari vs The State Of Jharkhand ... Opposite ... on 12 July, 2024
